title: Scaling AI Agents Without Breaking Reliability — Preeti Somal, Temporal

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk centers on Temporal as a durable execution runtime for AI agents, abstracting retries, state management, and crash recovery through workflows. Temporal is presented as infrastructure for software builders orchestrating agent workloads. The talk addresses both development velocity gains and production reliability for deployed agent systems. Prerequisites specify a developer audience familiar with distributed systems and agent architecture concepts. Recorded presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair in San Francisco. summary: Preeti Somal opens by establishing Temporal's reliability focus, symbolized by their tardigrade mascot—the most resilient animal known. Her goal is to convince the audience that Temporal is the right platform for building agentic AI applications. She frames agents as complex distributed systems that must cope with inherently unreliable LLMs, scale, and provide durability. Orchestration is core: workflows coordinate multiple processes, manage state over long periods, support human-in-the-loop interactions, and run in parallel while calling tools. The difficulty of debugging and testing agents in pre-production compounds these challenges. Temporal's mission is to outsource reliability and scalability so developers focus on business logic. The platform provides language-idiomatic SDKs (noting Python's surge past other languages in January), handles all plumbing code like retries, and has been in production for over a decade. Customer examples include Dust (agents on Temporal), Gorgias (customer service for brands like Reebok and Glossier), and mission-critical payments workloads. The architecture centers on a workflow abstraction written as code by developers. Key abstractions orchestrated include LLMs, chat history databases, and tools. Temporal concepts include signals (workflow input), queries, and activities (wrapped tools). All workflow history is stored for visibility and can be exported for compliance or debugging. The worker—developer code—runs in the customer's own environment, fitting existing CI/CD practices, while Temporal Cloud handles execution state, call stacks, failures, and retries. Impact claims include accelerating development to production in weeks, with one case study showing 6x feature delivery velocity improvement, and a consumer application scaling with events without handling scale logic. A ticket booking agent demo (available at booth G3) illustrates the workflow model. Temporal is open-source with code exchange examples and cloud credits for onboarding.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Temporal Reliability
sections.summary: Preeti Somal introduces herself as part of Temporal's engineering team, establishes Temporal's reliability focus through the tardigrade mascot metaphor, and states her goal of convincing the audience that Temporal is the right platform for agentic AI applications.

sections.title: Agent Challenges and Orchestration Needs
sections.summary: Frames agents as complex distributed systems needing orchestration, state management, human interaction, parallel execution, and tool calls. Highlights inherent LLM unreliability and difficulty of debugging and testing agents in pre-production.

sections.title: Temporal Solution, Maturity, and Customers
sections.summary: Describes Temporal's mission to outsource reliability and scalability, language-idiomatic SDKs with Python's surge, plumbing code handling, and over a decade in production. Customer examples include Dust, Gorgias (customer service for Reebok, Glossier), and mission-critical payments.

sections.title: Architecture and Workflow Abstraction
sections.summary: Contrasts pre-Temporal architecture (lots of interaction and error handling code) with Temporal's workflow abstraction. Key agent abstractions orchestrated: LLMs, chat history database, and tools. Workflow is a developer-focused, code-based tool.

sections.title: Impact Metrics
sections.summary: Claims accelerated development to production in weeks, 6x feature delivery velocity improvement, greater scale handled by Temporal Cloud, better sleep for engineers, and happier customers.

sections.title: Ticket Booking Agent Demo Walkthrough
sections.summary: Walks through a ticket booking agent architecture showing how Temporal wraps agent flow: workflows define flow as code, signals provide input, queries read state, activities wrap tools, and workflow history is stored and exportable. Worker code runs in customer environment; Temporal Cloud handles execution state and retries.

sections.title: Worker Code, Code Exchange, and Wrap-Up
sections.summary: Shows worker code screenshot, highlights Temporal as open-source with code exchange examples runnable locally or against cloud. Mentions cloud credits for onboarding and invites audience to booth G3.
